alice (eng-sec): Heads-up — customer ACME reported intermittent 401s after we did key rotation for the oauth service at 1918203000. Error: \"invalid signature\" and \"no matching JWK found for kid\". Can we triage? :eyes:

ben (support): Saw the alert. They started getting errors ~1918203200 and it flapped for ~5-10m. At first it looked like clock skew (exp/nbf) but logs show signature checks failing, specifically `kid` lookup failing in our verifier.

cara (cust-eng): We reproduced on their side — POSTs with new tokens succeed sometimes, but many requests return 401 JSON: `\{\"error\":\"invalid_signature\",\"message\":\"no matching key for kid: kp_abc123\"\}`. They also reported occasional 503s from our jwks endpoint during rotation.

deploy-bot: jwks-service deployed v2.1.7 at 1918202990 — rotation job kicked at 1918203005 — rotated keys kp_old -> kp_new with grace window=30s.

alice (eng-sec): Hypothesis: JWKS rotation + transient 5xx at jwks endpoint caused some verifier instances to still have stale cached keysets and then tokens signed with new kid failed. Also clock skew might make token look invalid on some edge nodes. Need repro steps and short-term mitigation for customer.

ben (support): Repro steps I used from the customer env:
```
# fetch token (signed by identity svc, kid=kp_new)
curl -sS -X POST https://id.acme.example.com/token -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' -u 'svc:secret' | jq -r '.access_token' > /tmp/tok
# attempt call to Redwood private endpoint with token
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /tmp/tok)" -X POST https://private.redwood.acme.internal/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# sometimes works, sometimes 401. When 401, verifier logs show:
# 2026-03-12T15:12:34Z verifier[verifier-7]: error verifying token: no matching JWK found for kid kp_abc123 (jwks cache age 600s)
```

cara (cust-eng): On their LB they observed some backend nodes had clocks ~90s slow. Combined with exp checks we saw `token is not valid yet` in a handful of requests.

alice (eng-sec): OK action items: 1) immediate customer mitigation: bump JWKS cache ttl to 30s on their private control plane OR flush JWKS cache on all verifier instances, and add leeway 120s for exp/nbf checks; 2) longer-term: make verifier fetch JWKS on kid-miss (with backoff) instead of failing fast; also treat 5xx from jwks endpoint as transient and retry.

ben (support): For private deployments we have `redwoodctl` helper — run:
```
redwoodctl auth jwks flush --scope all --cluster acme-prod
# verify cache age
redwoodctl auth jwks status --cluster acme-prod
```
I ran flush for ACME and they reported immediate drop in 401s.

jwks-bot: NOTE: jwks-cache metrics showed 503 spike at 1918203007-1918203012 and cache-evictions increased.

alice (eng-sec): Patch suggestion for runtime: on Verify(token):
1) try lookup key by kid in local cache
2) if not found, fetch JWKS (best-effort) and retry lookup
3) if fetching fails with 5xx/timeout, retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times, and only then fail auth
4) apply small leeway for exp/nbf (configurable, default 60s), but make it tenant-configurable for strict customers

Also add a rotation grace behavior: when keys rotate, keep old signing key in JWKS for at least `rotation_grace` seconds and expose that as part of the rotation API so verifiers can rely on it.

cara (cust-eng): Quick workaround we did client-side: when we get 401 invalid_signature and the token was just minted (<60s), we attempted to re-fetch token and replay the request — reduced failures. But obviously server-side fix is better.

ben (support): Logs I collected (verifier instance):
```
2026-03-12T15:12:34Z verifier[verifier-7]: jwt_verify error kid=kp_abc123 err=no_matching_jwk cache_age=600
2026-03-12T15:12:35Z verifier[verifier-7]: jwks_fetch status=503 url=https://jwks.internal.redwood/api/keys attempt=1
2026-03-12T15:12:35Z verifier[verifier-7]: jwt_verify error kid=kp_abc123 err=signature_mismatch
```

alice (eng-sec): Agree. Also we should make the JWKS client tolerant to stale caches for a short period rather than hard-fail on kid-miss. And add better observability: emit metric `jwt.kid_miss` and alert when it spikes.

jwks-bot: metric jwt.kid_miss spiked to 112 in 5m window at 1918203200.

alice (eng-sec): Proposed patch PR checklist:
- [ ] verifier: on kid-miss -> sync JWKS and retry
- [ ] jwks client: treat 5xx as retryable; implement jittered backoff
- [ ] config: jwks_cache_ttl default -> 60s (was 300s)
- [ ] add `rotation_grace` parameter to rotation API and ensure key remains discoverable for that window
- [ ] add `jwt.leeway` tenant config
- [ ] tests: simulate jwks 503 during rotation

ben (support): For the customer we already applied: JWKS cache flush + increased leeway to 120s + asked them to sync clocks. They saw success rate jump to 99.8% in 10m.

cara (cust-eng): Customer asks whether we can backport to their Dedicated fleet quickly — they have a security review but will accept a hotfix.

alice (eng-sec): I'll open an urgent PR and request a canary rollout to dedicated clusters. Ben — prepare rollback steps and the `redwoodctl` commands to flush jwks if anything goes wrong.

ben (support): Will do. Also adding runbook note in incidents repo: short-term steps, commands, and telem queries for jwt.kid_miss, jwks_5xx_rate, and verifier_cache_age.

alice (eng-sec): Thanks team. Follow-ups: PR link when created; add customer postmortem with timeline.

cara (cust-eng): Thx all, customer is happy for now. Will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
